ug.headline: Buyinza Adam urges NRM politicians to drop succession debate
ug.dek: The businessman says political organizing distracts citizens from wealth creation and efforts to reduce household poverty.
paragraphs: Buyinza Adam Luzindana, a businessman and former National Resistance Movement (NRM) youth leader, urged ruling-party politicians in Kampala to stop drawing Ugandans into early debate over who will succeed President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni. He said the focus should instead be wealth creation and reducing household poverty.

Luzindana, a former member of the NRM National Executive Council and former Kampala regional chairman of the NRM Youth League, said the succession question had been settled during the liberation struggle. He said its framework was established between 1982 and 1986 and finalized when the National Resistance Army captured state power. He also asserted that Museveni’s successor was known, without naming that person.

Luzindana urged politicians to give men, women and young people practical information about existing government wealth-creation programs. He said political faction-building was keeping some Ugandans from economic opportunities.

ug.headline: Stanbic Bank retains Uganda’s Bank of the Year title
ug.dek: The bank won four honours at Kampala’s 2nd Annual Bankers’ Awards, including Best Trade Finance Bank and two awards for its staff.
paragraphs: Stanbic Bank Uganda retained the Bank of the Year title for a second consecutive year, winning four awards at the 2nd Annual Bankers’ Awards in Kampala. The bank also received Best Trade Finance Bank, while two of its staff won individual honours.

Cathy Adengo, the bank’s head of sustainability, was named Banker of the Year. Mumba Kalifungwa, Stanbic’s chief executive, said the awards reflected the work of employees and customers’ trust in the bank.
The awards were presented by Henry Musasizi, Uganda’s state minister for finance, planning and economic development. Adengo also chairs the Uganda Bankers’ Association Sustainability Committee.

ug.headline: Uganda accountants urged to prepare sustainability reports and address stigma
ug.dek: At ACCA Uganda’s convention in Kampala, speakers called for early environmental data collection and an end to silence around mental health.
paragraphs: The Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) Uganda concluded its 2026 members convention at Speke Resort Munyonyo in Kampala, urging accounting professionals to address mental health stigma and prepare for sustainability reporting requirements. The two-day event brought finance professionals, business leaders and industry experts together to discuss changes in the profession.

Joseph Owolabi, Rubicola Consulting’s chief executive and a former ACCA president, urged organisations to collect environmental data early and run parallel reports before requirements become mandatory. He said reliable information would help businesses respond to regulators, investors and customers. Lydia Nankabirwa, who manages standards and technical services at Uganda’s Institute of Certified Public Accountants, said a committee would oversee a phased plan to implement international reporting standards and provide guidance to members.

Psychiatry professor Noeline Nakasujja of Makerere University said pressure to appear competent can keep professionals from acknowledging psychological difficulties. Convention discussions also covered green finance, carbon markets and sustainability in financial institutions’ lending, investment and risk management.

zw.headline: Zimbabwe's Premier Soccer League postpones two matches that could decide relegation
zw.dek: Agama and ZPC Kariba will now play their final fixtures at 2 pm on 25 November, after players struck over unpaid salaries.
paragraphs: Zimbabwe's Premier Soccer League (PSL), the country's top football league, has postponed Agama versus Highlanders and Herentals versus ZPC Kariba, rescheduling both final-day matches for 2 pm on Wednesday, 25 November. Players went on strike over unpaid salaries, and the Footballers Union of Zimbabwe issued a notice of withdrawal of labour. The fixtures had been scheduled for Saturday, 21 November.

The league's Emergency Committee said it made an exception to its usual practice of not rescheduling matches over club disputes because the results affect relegation. Agama are 15th with 31 points, in the relegation zone; ZPC Kariba are 14th with 33, two points clear. The league said both fixtures will kick off at the same time so that neither side gains an advantage by learning the other's result first.

Highlanders, on 45 points, and Herentals College, on 48, are safe. The title race between leaders Hardrock, on 70 points, and Scottland, on 68, and most other final-day matches remain scheduled as planned.

zw.headline: Mudenda tasks sports committee with seeking weekend Warriors matches
zw.dek: The speaker wants the committee to ask FIFA to move national-team games from weekdays, after Zimbabwe beat Equatorial Guinea 3-0 on Monday.
paragraphs: Zimbabwe’s National Assembly Speaker Jacob Mudenda has tasked the Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Sports with asking FIFA to consider moving national-team matches from weekdays to weekends. He said the change would allow more fans to attend.

Mudenda raised the issue after committee chairman Farai Jere congratulated the senior national soccer team for its 3-0 win over Equatorial Guinea in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier played on Monday. Jere said FIFA decides match dates, prompting Mudenda to assign him the task of engaging the governing body.

Mudenda said FIFA president Gianni Infantino should consider fans’ expectations, adding that football is a business and match scheduling should take the market into account. The committee’s next step is to approach FIFA.

cv.headline: Cape Verde's election commission proclaims Neves re-elected president
cv.dek: José Maria Neves won 63.96% of valid votes in the 15 November election, while turnout was the lowest on record for a presidential vote.
paragraphs: Cape Verde’s National Election Commission proclaimed José Maria Neves re-elected president after he won 82,621 votes, or 63.96% of valid ballots, in the 15 November election. The commission announced the final results in Praia on Saturday, 21 November, after completing the general count on Friday.

Joana Rosa placed second with 40,568 votes, or 31.40%, according to the results. Abstention reached 68.33%, the highest recorded in the country’s presidential elections. It stood at 65% in Cape Verde and 81% among voters abroad: of 76,452 registered overseas voters, 14,266 cast ballots.
Neves, who ran for re-election, will serve his second and final term from 2026 to 2031. His first term ran from 2021 to 2026.

cv.headline: CVsky adds flights to clear passengers disrupted by medical evacuations
cv.dek: The airline says about 92% of roughly 1,060 affected passengers were regularised by Friday, 20 November, after medical flights took priority.
paragraphs: Cape Verdean airline CVsky said medical evacuation flights disrupted commercial schedules on the Praia–São Filipe route and other domestic services. The urgent operations took priority, forcing changes to planned flights, the airline said in a statement.

About 1,060 passengers were affected, and roughly 92% had been regularised by Friday, 20 November. CVsky said it expected to raise that share to 95% through extra flights and increased capacity. It began operating a new aircraft on 19 November, adding seats for passengers still awaiting transport.

The airline said it was working to carry those passengers and restore normal operations. It also acknowledged that its communication and operational coordination need improvement, particularly when flights are cancelled, changed or rescheduled.

cv.headline: Cape Verde joins six states in submitting climate plans to the UN
cv.dek: The seven Portuguese-speaking countries account for 2,62% of global emissions, while Cape Verde faces frequent droughts and irregular rain.
paragraphs: Cape Verde and six other Portuguese-speaking countries have submitted updated climate plans, known as NDC 3.0, to the United Nations. The plans set emissions-reduction targets and adaptation measures under the Paris Agreement, which requires signatories to submit them every five years.

The countries accounted for 2,62% of global emissions in 2025, according to the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre emissions database, published in September 2026. Without Brazil, their share was 0,21%. The database puts Cape Verde’s emissions at 990,000 toneladas. It says the country faces frequent droughts and irregular rainfall.

The database compares countries using one methodology but excludes forests and land use, which can understate emissions where those are major sources. Most countries made their climate targets conditional on external support, according to the plans reviewed by Lusa.

cv.headline: Opinion: Cape Verde's trade fair shows activity but little urgency for change
cv.dek: Hélio Africano Varela, writing for Mindel Insite, says visitors to São Vicente's international trade fair found businesses at work but few new products or ways of working.
paragraphs: Hélio Africano Varela, writing in the Cape Verdean outlet Mindel Insite, describes visiting every stand at the Feira Internacional de Cabo Verde (FIC), a trade fair held on São Vicente, from technology to grogue. He found businesses, workers, products and services at work, and said the event reflects the country's economic pulse.

Varela says he left with a sense of sameness. He reports no sign of urgent change, no innovation driving new ideas, products or ways of working, and not enough evidence of a country preparing to compete in a rapidly changing world. He calls the problem a "bubble of lethargy", in which old models are applied to the present.

He points to the new political cycle, which has announced a commitment to the primary sector and industrialisation, and asks where the fair's response to that agenda was. The column does not name specific projects or commitments announced at the fair.

cv.headline: Lusophone University of Cape Verde awards Germano Almeida honorary doctorate
cv.dek: The novelist says Cape Verdean literature should preserve the people's memory while reflecting the country's changes and achievements.
paragraphs: The Lusophone University of Cape Verde awarded Germano Almeida, a Cape Verdean author with 23 published books, an honorary doctorate. Accepting the title, he said literature should remain tied to the memory and identity of the people while also following the country's transformations and achievements.

Almeida said he received the distinction as a literary figure, though much of his working life was spent in law and advocacy and he had taken part occasionally in politics. He described himself as a storyteller, tracing his writing to tales he heard as a child in Boa Vista and to people he knew in Cape Verde, especially in São Vicente, Santo Antão and Santiago.

He said that, after more than five decades of independence, the country should not be portrayed in literature only through drought, hunger, poverty and suffering. He credited Brazilian writer Jorge Amado's books with showing him that ordinary people had stories worth telling.

td.headline: Chad launches nationwide clean-up to fight dengue and malaria
td.dek: Prime Minister Allah Maye Halina began the campaign at Dembé market, with work targeting mosquito breeding sites, rubbish dumps and public spaces.
paragraphs: Chad’s Prime Minister, Allah Maye Halina, launched the National Sanitation Week on Saturday 21 November 2026 at Dembé market in N’Djaména’s 7th arrondissement. The campaign aims to step up the fight against dengue and malaria across the country, with clean-up work planned in the capital’s 10 arrondissements and all provinces.

The operation focuses on removing mosquito breeding sites, clearing illegal rubbish dumps and cleaning public spaces, Alwihda Info reported. After the launch, Halina visited several neighbourhoods and joined the work with a shovel. He urged residents to set aside every Saturday to clean neighbourhoods, schools and markets.
Government members, N’Djaména’s mayor, security forces, Red Cross volunteers and artists took part in the launch. The campaign’s slogan is “Put dengue out!”

td.headline: Wazouna Déby Foundation gives food and hygiene kits to 300 households
td.dek: The Chadian NGO distributed rice, oil, pasta, soap and mosquito nets in Machaga and Birbété to households identified with local leaders.
paragraphs: The Wazouna Déby Foundation, a national non-governmental organisation in Chad, distributed food and hygiene kits to 300 vulnerable households in Machaga and Birbété on Saturday 21 November 2026. The households were identified in collaboration with local leaders.

The food packages contained rice, oil and pasta, while the hygiene kits included soap and mosquito nets. Hamid Mahamat, the foundation’s national secretary-general, said the aid was intended to ease families’ daily needs and protect children, pregnant women and older people. He said the kits were meant to help prevent dengue and malaria.

The foundation’s delegation also visited Birbété, Ambetawa and Ada Sakine to extend the operation. Salima Ahmat Mbamta, who leads an association working with the foundation on breast, cervical and uterine cancer, praised its attention to women facing illness and poverty.

td.headline: Emi Koussi wins Chad's national oratory contest by 0.05 point

paragraphs: The University Emi Koussi won Chad’s third National Oratory Contest in N’Djamena on Saturday, 21 November 2026, scoring 16.85 out of 20. It beat the National Higher School of Information and Communication Technologies, known as ENASTIC, which scored 16.80.

The final was organised by the Association of Leaders for a Prosperous Chad and chaired by Youth and Sports Minister Naïr Abakar. ENASTIC argued for the need for great leaders, while Emi Koussi argued for more responsible citizens, under a debate theme asking what Chad needs.

Association president Youssouf Togoï described the contest as a forum for learning, critical thinking and civic training. Abakar said his ministry supported initiatives that promote young people’s talents.

dj.headline: Djibouti City prefecture clears vehicles and levels roads in three districts
dj.dek: The campaign also cleaned the EEGA (Escale Ecologique Grand Arrosage) canal and its banks, with police, road-agency and company equipment supporting the work.
paragraphs: Djibouti City's prefecture began a clean-up campaign across three sub-prefectures, removing abandoned vehicles, levelling urban roads and clearing the EEGA canal and its banks. In the 2nd arrondissement, sub-prefect Awaleh Chideh Farah supervised the removal of disused vehicles from main roads, including a road in Dar-el-Hanan; the vehicles were taken to an impound yard.

In Djebel, in the 3rd arrondissement, teams working under sub-prefect Isman Robleh Souldan levelled dirt roads to ease residents' movement and help the city's rubbish-collection trucks enter the neighbourhood. The Djibouti Roads Agency lent a grader and loader. In the 4th arrondissement, sub-prefect Awaleh Fod Mohamed's team cleared the canal and plastic waste with SOS Environnement; Chinese company CCECC supplied machinery. National police provided personnel and equipment for the vehicle operation.
The prefecture said the interventions would be progressively intensified, with priority given to the capital's main roads.

dj.headline: Djibouti proposes permanent secretariat for African official gazettes
dj.dek: A forum is due to consider a cooperation charter, shared publication standards and a database for laws issued across the continent.
paragraphs: Djibouti is seeking a permanent secretariat to coordinate cooperation among African official gazettes, following the first forum in 2025. The government-organised forum is being held under the patronage of President Ismail Omar Guelleh.

Organisers say participants are expected to sign a cooperation charter and adopt a “Declaration of Djibouti”. The proposed secretariat would track commitments and keep dialogue going between member states. The forum is also due to advance shared publication standards and links between national platforms, which currently do not communicate with one another.

The discussions include artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and electronic archiving. Djibouti says its e-JO platform has digitised all its published legal texts dating to 1901 and offers search and alerts for new texts; artificial-intelligence tools are due to be added.

sz.headline: Eswatini central bank holds discount rate at 7%
sz.dek: The decision keeps the prime lending rate at 10.50% as October inflation rises to 3.4%.
paragraphs: The Central Bank of Eswatini kept its discount rate at 7% on Friday, leaving the prime lending rate at 10.50% until its next monetary policy meeting. The decision came as headline inflation accelerated by 0.5 percentage points to 3.4% in October, from 2.9% in September.

The bank’s Monetary Policy Consultative Committee chose not to tighten monetary policy, in line with economists’ expectations. The Central Statistical Office said monthly inflation rose to 0.9% in October from 0.2% in September, with transport and housing-related costs driving pressure on household spending.
Transport inflation reached 6.9% annually, while housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels rose 6.8%. Food and non-alcoholic beverages recorded annual inflation of negative 0.1%.

sz.headline: Eswatini pension funds’ combined quarterly surplus falls to E59.2 million
sz.dek: The Public Enterprises Unit links the decline from about E800 million to oil, energy and defence-stock volatility during the quarter.
paragraphs: Eswatini’s two biggest pension funds, the Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF) and the Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF), reported a combined quarterly surplus of E59.2 million, down from about E800 million. The Public Enterprises Unit (PEU), which supervises parastatals for the Finance Ministry, attributed the fall to the US/Israel war against Iran.

The PEU said PSPF’s net surplus dropped to E4.86 million from E1.52 billion in the previous quarter, alongside equity revaluation losses of E680.60 million, compared with gains of E840.71 million. ENPF recorded a surplus of E54.3 million, down from E175.6 million. The unit said the conflict amplified volatility in oil, energy equities and defence-related stocks, affecting investment performance.

The PEU said both funds remained financially sound: PSPF’s accumulated funds rose slightly to E43.001 billion, while ENPF’s funding level remained 1.07 times. Combined investment income rose to E950.22 million from E803.35 million; total expenditure increased from E557.76 million to E664.69 million.

sz.headline: Agama’s relegation decider delayed until November 25 after wage dispute
sz.dek: The Zimbabwe Premier Soccer League postponed both relegation fixtures after unpaid wages led Highlanders players to refuse travel and Agama’s squad to protest.
paragraphs: Agama, the Zimbabwe club of Eswatini international Newman “Strong” Philiso, will play its relegation decider against Highlanders on November 25 after unpaid wages disrupted Saturday’s fixtures. Highlanders players refused to travel to the match at Wadzanai Stadium, while Agama’s players had also protested over unpaid dues.

The Zimbabwe Premier Soccer League Emergency Committee said the disputes could not be resolved amicably and postponed both matches. Agama have 31 points and must beat Highlanders while ZPC Kariba, on 33, lose to Herentals; a ZPC Kariba draw would leave Agama needing a 13-goal win. The fixtures are scheduled for 2pm and will be played simultaneously.

Highlanders chairman Kindman Ndlovu said players had gone four months without salaries; chief executive Denzil Mnkandla put the arrears at two to three months. The club said the dispute could affect preparations for the Chibuku Super Cup final.

sz.headline: Eswatini's state university targets 200 solar installer trainees a year
sz.dek: The programme has certified 78 participants so far, and a construction industry council has committed E450 000 to it.
paragraphs: The University of Eswatini plans to train up to 200 solar installation artisans each year, as it seeks to address a shortage of skilled workers and create jobs. Pro Vice-Chancellor Henry Gadaga announced the target at a certificate ceremony at the university on November 20, 2026.

63 participants received certificates after completing the second cohort, bringing the total trained since the programme began to 78. The first cohort of 15 was certified in October 2025. The training is run with the Construction Industry Council, which committed E450 000 through its STEMPower project.

Gadaga said approximately 80% of Eswatini's electricity was imported, and that the Government's Energy Master Plan set out a path to energy independence by 2034. The council's Catherine Chikosenu-Motsa said its investment was prompted by rising installation of solar systems on buildings and the need for safety and quality standards.

sz.headline: CAF raises WAFCON winners’ prize to about E34 million
sz.dek: The increase comes as Eswatini’s senior women’s team has yet to reach the tournament finals or advance beyond the COSAFA group stage.
paragraphs: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) raised the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) winners’ prize to US2 million (about E34 million) in 2026, up from US200 000 (approximately E3.4 million) in 2021. The announcement came at CAF’s 48th Ordinary General Assembly in Abuja, Nigeria, on Saturday.

Eswatini’s senior women’s team, Sitsebe, have never reached the WAFCON finals and were not among the 16 countries that contested this year’s edition in Morocco. The overall prize fund has risen from US975 000 (E16.6 million) to US5.8 million (approximately E98.6 million), according to CAF.

At the COSAFA Women’s Championship in February, Sitsebe earned one point in three Group B matches and exited after a 2-1 loss to Zambia. The Eswatini Football Association faces the task of strengthening women’s football and preparing the team for international competition.

ga.headline: Gabon prepares to split its state water and power utility by December
ga.dek: The government says no Gabonese employee should lose a job as officials work through contracts, debt and asset transfers before the split takes effect.
paragraphs: Gabon is preparing to divide the Société d'énergie et d'eau du Gabon (SEEG), the state water and electricity operator, into two companies by December 2026: Électricité du Gabon (EDG) for power and La Gabonaise des Eaux (GDE) for water. Vice-President of the Government Hermann Immongault received Water and Energy Minister Olivier Mouckocko, along with SEEG's board chairman and managing director, on 19 November to review progress.

Minister Olivier Mouckocko said the instruction from President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema is that no Gabonese employee should lose a job by the end of the process. The meeting also sought approval for a committee to oversee the steps needed before separation. SEEG is a private-law company governed by OHADA, the business law framework covering much of francophone Africa, so the transfer must clarify employment contracts, responsibilities and asset transfers.

Officials said they must first establish the real level of SEEG's debt, take an inventory of state assets held in the company and give assurances to its shareholders. Continued dialogue with staff and social partners was identified as essential to the operation's success.

ga.headline: Gabon delivers first chicks to farms under poultry plan
ga.dek: The agriculture minister received 37 600 day-old chicks in Libreville from a first order of 262 400 due to arrive by 17 December.
paragraphs: Gabon received 37 600 day-old chicks at Libreville’s Léon-Mba International Airport on 19 November, beginning deliveries under its emergency poultry plan. The chicks, imported from France, are intended to expand domestic production of broiler chickens ahead of a ban on broiler imports.

Agriculture Minister Pacôme Kossy said the first shipment was part of an order for 262 400 chicks, to be received and distributed by 17 December. The deliveries are for 79 poultry farms selected from 150 applicants. The state purchasing agency has also ordered 1,2 million tonnes of animal feed, and its director, Théophile Boutamba, said nearly 80% of the farms had already received feed.
Interior Minister Edgard Moukoumbi said security forces would accompany chick deliveries to farms. A wider order covers 3 million birds; the government adopted the poultry plan in February 2026.

paragraphs: Gabon’s public vocational training centres are holding their entrance exam on Saturday 21 November, with 5 880 candidates expected, according to Gabon Review. The National Agency for Vocational Training and Education (ANFEP) is organising the session after the exam was rescheduled.

In Libreville, candidates will sit the tests at the Basile-Ondimba school complex and Omar-Bongo University. Mathematics is scheduled for the morning, followed by French and general knowledge. Organisers said the tests will take place simultaneously at the centres concerned.

An organising official said candidates will not be admitted after the examinations begin, urging them to arrive on time because the tests use multiple-choice questions. The exam had originally been announced for 16 November before being moved for practical and technical reasons.

ga.headline: Isuzu trains 24 Gabon truck drivers to cut breakdowns
ga.dek: The two-day Libreville course covered driving, maintenance and road safety, with special attention to onboard systems many drivers did not know.
paragraphs: Isuzu Motors International, Sodim TP and Gabon’s transport ministry trained 24 Isuzu truck drivers in Libreville on 19 and 20 November, covering vehicle operation, maintenance and road safety. Experts sent from Dubai led the practical sessions, the second stage of a programme launched in March 2025.

The drivers practised braking, clutch use, gear changes, load management and cornering, and learned about onboard safety systems. Isuzu commercial director Collins Djimmo Tima said many drivers had not known those systems were fitted. Sodim TP’s Izzard Biyang Ndong said customers complained about clutch problems because drivers did not follow the supplier’s instructions.
Participants Paul Koumenic of ETS Christelle & Filles and Seuntio Colince of Makaco Sarl said the training showed them how their driving practices had contributed to wear and repair costs.

ga.headline: Port-Gentil police hold students as school imposes exclusion

paragraphs: Police in Port-Gentil have taken students from Ogoula Mbeye Evangelical high school into custody after videos described as obscene circulated on 19 November 2026. The school’s disciplinary council has also excluded the students identified in the recordings.

Pierre Onanga Ossounda, the provincial academic director for Ogooué-Maritime, said the school director, students involved and their parents were called in and heard. He said the academic directorate notified its ministry hierarchy and the national directorate for private education of the Evangelical Church of Gabon. The exclusion’s duration has not been set; the school’s official report is pending.

Onanga Ossounda said the students were taken to Port-Gentil’s central police station for the investigation. He said school rules and decrees 0857, 0858 and 0859 provide for disciplinary measures, and warned that repeat conduct would bring disciplinary and judicial sanctions.

gm.headline: Gambian media study finds ruling party led TV coverage before vote
gm.dek: The ruling National People's Party held up to 91.3% of party airtime on state broadcaster GRTS, while the opposition United Democratic Party's press mentions rose.
paragraphs: A baseline media report on Gambia found the ruling National People's Party (NPP) took most party-related television airtime in the six months before the official campaign for the 5 December 2026 presidential election. The analysis covered 316 evening news bulletins from state broadcaster GRTS and private stations QTV (Quantum Television) and Star TV between April and September.

On GRTS, the NPP held 91.3% of party airtime in April to June and 85.6% in July to September, while President Adama Barrow alone accounted for roughly 32% of tracked airtime in both periods. The report, published by Gambian computer scientist Muhammed Njie of the analytics firm Cubixio, counts a politician's airtime toward their party, including coverage of official duties.

In press articles mentioning a party or leader, the United Democratic Party (UDP) rose from 22.5% to 33.5% of such articles between the two quarters. The report cautions that the mix of outlets changed between quarters, so the figures should not be read as a direct like-for-like trend.

gm.headline: Bensouda vows to end groundnut price ceilings if elected
gm.dek: The Unite Party candidate says removing the limits would help farmers earn more, alongside plans for local manufacturing and healthcare.
paragraphs: Talib Ahmed Bensouda, the Unite Party presidential candidate, has promised to remove price ceilings on groundnuts if elected in The Gambia’s December 2026 election. He made the pledge during a campaign tour of the Central River Region, after earlier stops in the North Bank.

Bensouda said farmers would be able to earn more from their produce without the ceilings. His 66-point agenda also proposes encouraging local manufacturing and using duties and tariffs to discourage imports of goods that can be made in The Gambia. He cited furniture imports worth roughly D500 million a year, including about D100 million in government purchases, and said local production could create jobs for young people.

He also proposed shifting healthcare spending from buildings towards medicines, trained staff and equipment, and offering reintegration programmes for people returning from irregular migration. Cape Verde’s tourism growth was a comparison he cited while proposing heritage tourism and investment in higher-end tourism.

gm.headline: Maka Masireh residents press candidates for roads and basic services
gm.dek: The remote Upper River Region village says a difficult road journey and limited local health care leave residents struggling to reach essential services.
paragraphs: Residents of Maka Masireh, a village in Gambia’s Upper River Region, are asking presidential candidates to address poor roads, limited health care and lack of clean water ahead of the December election. The village is about seven kilometres from the Pasamas-Laminkoto highway, and its connecting track becomes nearly impassable during the rainy season.

Resident Kaddy Dampha said completing the road and improving access to services were urgent needs. Another resident, Amadou Camara, said health facilities have little medicine beyond paracetamol. Villagers travel to Baja Kunda for medical care and necessities, while residents also want support for women’s gardens and a local market.
Young resident Ma Koyoi Kandeh said youths want a football pitch. Residents say they hope candidates will turn campaign promises into action after the polls.

gm.headline: Analyst questions Team Gambia's absence from opposition alliances
gm.dek: Political analyst Lamin Juwara says he expected the group to join a larger bloc before nominations for the December presidential election.
paragraphs: Political analyst Lamin Juwara has questioned why the Team Gambia Grand Coalition has not joined one of the larger opposition alliances ahead of Gambia's December presidential election. Speaking on the Brunch show on Kerr Fatou on Saturday, he said he had expected the group to seek a place in a potential coalition before nominations.

Juwara said the individuals behind Team Gambia have played a pivotal role in alliance building throughout the country's political history. He said the No-To-Alliance's main bargaining chip is the return of former President Yahya Jammeh, and suggested the group would likely demand that return without accountability or conditions.

He said a deal between the United Democratic Party (UDP) and the No-To-Alliance would be a major move for the election and for transitional justice, but that trust between the parties on such a deal was highly volatile. He also questioned how much influence the alliance's candidate, Almameh Gibba, could exert alone, and whether he would follow instructions relayed from Jammeh through WhatsApp audio messages.
gm.body:
Political analyst Lamin Juwara has questioned why the Team Gambia Grand Coalition has not joined one of the larger opposition alliances ahead of Gambia's December presidential election. Speaking on the Brunch show on Kerr Fatou on Saturday, he said he had expected the group to seek a place in a potential coalition before nominations.

Juwara said the individuals behind Team Gambia have played a pivotal role in alliance building throughout the country's political history. He said the No-To-Alliance's main bargaining chip is the return of former President Yahya Jammeh, and suggested the group would likely demand that return without accountability or conditions.

He said a deal between the United Democratic Party (UDP) and the No-To-Alliance would be a major move for the election and for transitional justice, but that trust between the parties on such a deal was highly volatile. He also questioned how much influence the alliance's candidate, Almameh Gibba, could exert alone, and whether he would follow instructions relayed from Jammeh through WhatsApp audio messages.

gn.headline: Bel Air Mining barge collision leaves two Guinean fishermen dead off Boffa
gn.dek: The bodies of the two fishermen missing after their canoe was caught in the barge's nets were recovered after almost 48 hours of search.
paragraphs: Two artisanal fishermen who went missing after a bauxite barge operated by Bel Air Mining collided with their canoe off Boffa were found dead, the national artisanal fishing federation said on Saturday. The accident happened on the night of 18 to 19 November off the port of Cap Verga, in Boffa prefecture, when the barge became entangled in the fishermen's nets and dragged their canoe towards the vessel.

Fodé Idrissa Kallo, communications officer of the Fédération nationale de la pêche artisanale de Guinée (FENAPAG), said one fisherman jumped into the water and was rescued, while the other two were pulled under the barge. One body was found on Friday and the second on Saturday morning, after several hours of searching each day.

Kallo said a barge of the same company had run over a fishing boat on 13 February 2026, killing a fisherman, and that the then ministers of fisheries and mines visited the site afterwards. He called for the maritime rules to be enforced, for the channel the mining firms are creating to be marked with buoys, and for each company's navigation plan to be shared with the fishing community.

gn.headline: African guarantee fund plans sector-focused business fairs in Guinea
gn.dek: The fund says it will discuss further editions with Guinean authorities after the first event outside the West African monetary union.
paragraphs: The 12th Banks and SMEs Fair for the West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA) ended in Conakry on Saturday, 21 November, after two days of discussions on financing small businesses. Guinea, which is not a UEMOA member, hosted the event for the first time at the initiative of the African Fund for Guarantee and Economic Cooperation (FAGACE).

FAGACE president Ngueto Tiraïna Yambaye said the fair brought banks, microfinance institutions and businesses together to build confidence and speed up financing. Atlantic Microfinance network officer Adama Yaya Diallo said her institution made contacts with companies that could qualify for funding.

Yambaye said FAGACE would discuss special editions with Guinean authorities and its administrators, potentially holding several fairs each year. He said they could focus on financing agriculture and livestock.

gn.headline: Guinea’s CBG receives ESG Gold 2026 award at Hanoi conference

gn.headline: Guinea's BCEIP sets sights on expanding beyond its borders
gn.dek: The 30-year-old company says it wants to deepen its contribution to Guinea's economy while extending its activities abroad.
paragraphs: BCEIP, a Guinean company providing recruitment, outsourced human-resources management and other services, marked 30 years in Conakry on Saturday, 21 November. The company was founded in 1996 and also works in security, property management, home assistance and agribusiness.

Managing director Mohamed Yiremba Sidibé said BCEIP helps companies recruit staff and secure their operations in Guinea. At the anniversary ceremony, the company presented its record and future plans, and Sidibé said its strategy includes continued training for workers, both inside and outside the company.

Sidibé said BCEIP had faced regulatory and social difficulties, including challenges in meeting labour law requirements. He said the company intends to strengthen its contribution to Guinea’s economy and expand its activities beyond the country.

lr.headline: Liberia offers 15 offshore oil blocks to investors
lr.dek: The licensing round covers 12 blocks in the Liberia Basin and three in the Harper Basin, with letters of intent due April 15, 2027.
paragraphs: Liberia opened a licensing round in October offering 15 offshore petroleum blocks to investors, as world leaders negotiated ocean protections at the United Nations climate talks (COP31) in Türkiye. The Liberia Petroleum Regulatory Authority is offering 12 blocks in the Liberia Basin and three in the Harper Basin.

Companies interested in the 2026 Offshore Direct Negotiation Licensing Round have until April 15, 2027, to submit letters of intent. Liberia's 2035 climate commitment also calls for two marine protected areas and four co-managed fisheries areas, while coastal fishing and fish processing provide food, jobs and income.

Residents of West Point say they have not been directly consulted about offshore oil and gas plans. The locations of the proposed protected and fisheries areas, and whether they overlap with petroleum blocks, remain unresolved.

ly.headline: Libya's state oil firm reports 30,792,522 USD loss from Hamada pipeline closure
ly.dek: The National Oil Corporation says an armed group's shutdown of the pipeline has cut crude output by 302,778 barrels over more than 20 days.
paragraphs: Libya's National Oil Corporation said the closure of the Hamada pipeline by an armed Libyan group has cost 302,778 barrels of crude oil, valued at 30,792,522 USD, over more than 20 days. It reported an average daily loss of 14,418 barrels, equal to 1,470,636 USD in revenue.

The shutdown affects the Al-Hamada fields, known as NC5 and NC8, and the Al-Tahara field, known as NC4, all operated by the Arabian Gulf Oil Company. The corporation said the losses are based on the average crude price and are in addition to fixed operating costs at those fields.
The corporation urged relevant authorities and citizens to work toward reopening the pipeline and to end attacks on oil facilities. It said the closure has also caused a decline in production.

ly.headline: Libya ranks second in Africa for central bank gold reserves
ly.dek: Algeria leads the continent with 173.6 tonnes, and the top four holders together hold 575.8 tonnes, a World Gold Council tally cited in a 20 November report.
paragraphs: Libya holds 146.7 tonnes of gold in its central bank reserves, placing it second in Africa behind Algeria's 173.6 tonnes, according to World Gold Council figures.

Egypt ranks third with 130 tonnes and South Africa fourth with 125.5 tonnes. Tanzania is fifth with 39.6 tonnes, a figure announced by its minerals minister. Libya has almost no industrial gold mining, so the Central Bank of Libya has built its stock through purchases, including 30 tonnes bought in 2023.
A bne IntelliNews report of 20 November put the four leading countries' combined holdings at 575.8 tonnes, more than 14 times Tanzania's reported figure.

ly.headline: Libyan inspector says counterfeit medicines enter daily
ly.dek: Abu Bakr Marwan says his Souq Al-Jumaa team is short of resources and has spent seven years inspecting food and medicines.
paragraphs: Abu Bakr Marwan, head of the Food and Drug Monitoring Unit in Souq Al-Jumaa, Tripoli, said counterfeit medicines, carcinogenic pesticides and substandard food enter Libya every day. He said his team would continue inspections despite limited resources.

Marwan said he and his colleagues had carried out field visits during his seven years as an inspector, but that the corruption network exceeded their capabilities. He attributed the problem to weak laws, smuggling through insecure borders and ports, and food security being left to people driven by self-interest.
He called for a comprehensive system, stricter laws and real resources to confront the problem.

mg.headline: Madagascar court moves Ambohimalaza poisoning trial toward former health minister
mg.dek: Lawyers for the civil parties want the former health minister, doctors and gendarmes called as witnesses over the response to the poisoning that killed at least 35 people.
paragraphs: Madagascar's Ordinary Criminal Court in Anosy is weighing calls to summon former health minister Zely Arivelo Randriamanantany in the Ambohimalaza poisoning trial. At least 35 people died after a birthday party on 14 June 2025 in Imerinkasinina, most of them young people.

The prosecutor's general office said the steps needed to issue the summonses were under way. Hospital officials, doctors from the Hôpital Joseph Ravoahangy Andrianavalona (HJRA), a state hospital in Antananarivo, and gendarmes who investigated the case could also be called. Lawyers want the court to examine the treatment protocols, the resources deployed and why some victims were not evacuated abroad for care.

Tojo Rahamefy, one of 14 survivors, told the court he still depends on breathing assistance and is waiting for surgery abroad after selling part of his property to pay for treatment. The trial resumes on Monday, 23 November.

mg.headline: Madagascar civil society groups prepare joint statement on election process
mg.dek: The planned declaration would challenge the conduct of the 9 and 10 November electoral consultations at the Ivato International Conference Centre.
paragraphs: Several civil society organisations and members in Madagascar are preparing a joint statement on the electoral consultations held on 9 and 10 November at the Ivato International Conference Centre, according to Madagascar Tribune. The declaration has not yet been made public and could be released as early as next week.

The groups are expected to raise reservations about how the consultations were conducted and about institutional decisions that could shape the country's political future. They are also expected to press for stronger guarantees of transparency and independence in the mechanisms overseeing the coming polls, including a constitutional referendum announced before the 2027 elections.

The authorities of the Refoundation process intend to keep the first elections on schedule for 2027, despite persistent questions about how they will be organised. The organisations have not yet formally announced their initiative.

mg.headline: Germany offers Madagascar €56.5 million in development grants
mg.dek: The funding includes €46.4 million for financial cooperation and €10.1 million for technical support across several sectors.
paragraphs: Germany pledged €56.5 million in grants for development projects in Madagascar after intergovernmental negotiations in Antananarivo on 19 and 20 November 2026. The funding is intended for financial and technical cooperation.

Germany’s embassy said €46.4 million would go to financial cooperation and €10.1 million to technical support. Planned areas include rural electrification, agricultural value chains, protected-area management, forest restoration, local development and decentralisation.

The funding is linked to Madagascar’s transition roadmap, including the organisation of free, inclusive and fair elections and respect for freedom of expression and assembly, political dialogue, anti-corruption measures, the rule of law and human rights. Germany also plans technical support for the mining sector with Madagascar’s Mines Ministry; a German geosciences institute is expected to open an office in the country.

mg.dek: MEDEF International and Madagascar's business group met government officials in Antananarivo on water, sanitation and waste management as French lawmaker Bruno Fuchs held.
paragraphs: French and Malagasy business groups discussed urban water supply, sanitation and waste management with government officials in Antananarivo during a joint working visit by MEDEF International and the Groupement des entreprises de Madagascar (GEM). The talks also covered clearing the capital's canals, transport and youth training.

The delegations were led by Gautier Philippe, director general of MEDEF International, and Francis Rabarijohn, president of GEM. Economy and Finance Minister Herinjatovo Aimé Ramiarison led the government side at a meeting at the Mahazoarivo state palace, and the French delegation also met private-sector representatives to identify possible partnerships and investment.

French lawmaker Bruno Fuchs, who chairs the French National Assembly's Foreign Affairs Committee, separately met President Michaël Randrianirina, Prime Minister Mamitiana Rajaonarison and Refoundation Minister Hanitra Razafimanantsoa. The talks covered bilateral relations, institutional issues and economic prospects.

mw.headline: Malawi motorists sleep at filling stations as fuel queues deepen
mw.dek: Drivers have reportedly spent days and nights waiting for fuel through October and November as shortages persist across the country.
paragraphs: Motorists in Malawi have been spending days and nights at filling stations while waiting for fuel, as shortages deepened through October and November. The queues have turned petrol stations into overnight campgrounds, with pumps running dry in parts of the country.

The report links the shortage to depleted foreign-exchange reserves, costly fuel imports, a weakening kwacha and logistical bottlenecks. It says motorists and businesses face rising costs, while fuel was priced at about $3.23 a litre in October rankings, putting Malawi at the top of the African list cited by the report.

The article also raises allegations of corruption involving billions of kwacha and senior government officials, but gives no findings or official response. It contrasts Malawi’s shortage with Sudan’s war-related crisis and Niger’s refinery shortfall.

mw.headline: Malawi's ruling party blames fuel shortages on US-Iran conflict
mw.dek: Jappie Mhango, vice-president of the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) for the North, said the shortages stem from turmoil in the Middle East, not the party's own decisions.
paragraphs: Jappie Mhango, vice-president of the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) for the North, blamed Malawi's fuel shortages on conflict between the United States and Iran, telling supporters at an interface meeting in Chitipa District that the crisis was driven by events beyond the party's control.

Mhango said the party had promised Malawians reliable access to food, foreign exchange, fuel and fertiliser, and claimed progress in some areas. He cited food availability and increased funding for local projects through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) as evidence of delivery, and said efforts were underway to resolve the fuel shortages.

The gathering also welcomed two defectors: former Chitipa Wenya MP Davis Ng'ambi, and Isaac Mwepa, a former deputy director of public relations for the Malawi Congress Party (MCP). Mwepa said he was drawn to the DPP by its strong and decisive leadership and its visible development projects.

mw.headline: Malawi airport tells passengers to arrive four hours early amid check-in fault
mw.dek: Kamuzu International Airport has used manual check-in since Nov. 17 after heavy rain and strong winds disrupted its automated service.
paragraphs: Passengers travelling through Kamuzu International Airport in Malawi have been told to arrive at least four hours before departure after a technical fault disrupted check-in. Airport authorities have switched from automated processing to manual check-in, increasing the risk of delays.

Airport Development Limited (ADL), which manages Malawi’s airports, said heavy rainfall and strong winds affected the area on Nov. 17 and caused the fault. Spokesperson Wezzie Gondwe Lawrence said ADL was working to repair the system and restore normal operations. Passengers have also been asked to bring required travel documents, including valid passports and visas.
ADL gave no date for the return of automated check-in. The four-hour advisory is intended to give travellers time to complete the manual process.

mw.headline: Mutharika gives K5 million to women journalists' association
mw.dek: The Association of Women in Media is holding its elective annual general meeting in Mponela, Dowa, where members are choosing new leaders.
paragraphs: President Arthur Peter Mutharika has donated K5 million to the Association of Women in Media (AWOME) as the organisation holds its elective annual general meeting in Mponela, Dowa.

Speaking on his behalf on Saturday, Presidential Press Secretary Cathy Maulidi praised women journalists for amplifying marginalised voices on maternal health, girls' education and rural development. AWOME Board of Trustees member Jayne Gogodus urged more women in media to join the association and elect leaders able to advance its vision.

Christina Mkutumula, Deputy Director of Information in the Ministry of Information and Communications Technology, reaffirmed the government's commitment to media freedom and to initiatives strengthening the capacity, safety and leadership of women journalists.

mw.headline: LUANAR honours biopesticide researcher at excellence awards
mw.dek: Dr Trust Donga’s natural pest-control formulations have cleared Malawi’s agricultural technology review and are in final registration.
paragraphs: Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources (LUANAR) honoured students, researchers, innovators and academic departments at its 2025/26 Vice-Chancellor’s Excellence Awards on 20 November 2026. The awards covered student academic performance, innovation, resource mobilisation, research publications and departmental research productivity.

Dr Trust Donga won the Outstanding Excellence in Innovation Award for developing natural biopesticides and agroecological crop-protection methods. LUANAR said the products are intended to help smallholder farmers tackle pests including fall armyworm and insects that damage stored crops. The university said her formulations had been reviewed and cleared by Malawi’s Agricultural Technology Clearing Committee, with support from its Technology Transfer Office.

The products are progressing through final registration with the Pesticides Control Board. Vice-Chancellor Professor Emmanuel Kaunda said the awards recognised work in research, innovation and academic performance.

ml.headline: Mali's cargo council reports nearly CFA80 billion in savings
ml.dek: Transport Minister Madina Sissoko said measures agreed with Dakar and Abidjan port authorities reduced or cancelled penalties on Malian goods.
paragraphs: Mali's Council of Shippers, the Conseil Malien des Chargeurs (CMC), reported nearly CFA80 billion in savings for cargo owners after measures at the ports of Dakar and Abidjan reduced or cancelled penalties on Malian goods. Transport and Infrastructure Minister Madina Sissoko presided over the opening of the council's 17th consular assembly in Bamako on Saturday, 21 November.

Sissoko credited the savings to government efforts coordinated with the CMC and other parties, which secured exceptional relief on demurrage and parking charges. The assembly is reviewing the council's 2026 activity report and budget execution, along with earlier recommendations.
Members are also due to adopt the CMC's activity programme and proposed budget for 2027. The council's electronic cargo-tracking platform, known as CIWARA, has been operating since 18 September 2026.

ml.headline: Mali brings 756 fuel tankers to Bamako under military escort
ml.dek: The convoy takes the total delivered to the capital in November to 2 261, according to Mali's trade and competition directorate.
paragraphs: A convoy of 756 fuel tankers reached parking areas in Bamako in the night of Friday to Saturday 21 November, escorted by Mali's armed forces. The arrival brought the number of tankers sent to the capital during the first three weeks of November to 2 261, according to the Directorate-General for Trade, Consumption and Competition.

The convoy arrived at about 3 h 05, the directorate said. It was the third delivery this month, after 665 tankers on 7 November and 840 on 14 November. The deliveries are intended to supply fuel to Bamako's service stations.
The armed forces accompanied the latest convoy along its route to the capital, a role the directorate said is important for protecting the convoys and keeping supply moving.

ml.headline: Mali opens regional police headquarters in Koulikoro
ml.dek: The national-budget project adds a solar-powered, water-independent base for the force in a city facing security pressure along its corridor with Bamako.
paragraphs: Mali’s security minister, Daoud Aly Mohammedine, inaugurated a new regional police headquarters and the regional director’s on-call residence in Koulikoro on 20 November. The R+1 complex, built on half a hectare in Katibougou Extension, was funded entirely from the national budget and includes solar power and an autonomous water well.

The regional police directorate had been operating in part of the governor’s offices, according to the Malian Press and Publicity Agency. Governor Lamine Kapory Sanogo said Koulikoro’s proximity to Bamako and population movement create security challenges. The new headquarters joins two police stations and a rapid-intervention police company already operating in the city.

Mohammedine said the building was intended to improve police working conditions and support their duties. He cited crime, cybercrime, organised cross-border crime, drug trafficking, human trafficking and terrorist threats among the security challenges facing the country.

ml.headline: Mali helps return 130 people to Burkina Faso and Ghana
ml.dek: Burkina Faso sent a bus for 123 people on 19 November, while Ghana arranged transport for seven of its citizens.
paragraphs: Malian authorities helped transport 130 people from gathering sites in Mali to Burkina Faso and Ghana, according to a statement dated 20 November. Burkina Faso sent a bus from the Quinzindougou site on 19 November for 123 people; Ghana arranged transport for seven of its citizens.

The statement said 455 people remained at the Quinzindougou youth centre, down from 564 the previous day. They included 260 Beninese, 190 Togolese, two Burkinabè, two Nigeriens and one Guinean. Another 20 Burkinabè remained at the Kouremalé site.
Mali is consulting the countries concerned to organise returns for those still at the sites. The crisis coordination centre urged communities to help locate and direct people who remain dispersed.

ml.headline: Club Tamani looks at the veil that marks young Tuareg women's lives
ml.dek: Studio Tamani's programme traced where the practice began, when it starts in a girl's life and what it signifies in Tuareg society.
paragraphs: Club Tamani, a programme of Studio Tamani, examined the practice of young Tuareg women wearing the veil during the third International Tuareg Crafts Week, held at Mali's National Museum. The broadcast asked how the practice began, when it enters a young woman's life and what its stages are.
Mohamed Elmaouloud Ag Hamid, president of the Timidwa association and director of the National Tuareg Crafts Week, joined the programme to explain the tradition and its meaning in Tuareg society.
The full programme was broadcast on 20 November 2026 and is available to listen to on Studio Tamani's website.

mr.headline: Mauritania presents civil service pension reform options to unions
mr.dek: Prime Minister Moktar Ould Diay said the study diagnosed the scheme and set out choices balancing financial sustainability with social fairness.
paragraphs: Mauritania’s Prime Minister Moktar Ould Diay presented findings from a study of civil servants’ pension reform to union leaders and representatives of independent unions on Friday. The meeting focused on the study’s proposed options for changing the scheme.

Ould Diay said the study had produced a full diagnosis of the pension system. He said its scenarios would allow officials to choose a formula balancing financial sustainability with social fairness. The prime minister’s office said participants received a detailed presentation of each option’s financial and administrative effects.
The report does not specify which option the government will choose or when a decision will be made.

mr.headline: Mauritania sets border priorities in West African migration process
mr.dek: At a Dakar conference, the foreign ministry’s secretary-general called for regional cooperation and outlined controls on migration data and document fraud.
paragraphs: Mauritania’s foreign ministry secretary-general, Ambassador Daman Hammer, set out the country’s migration priorities at a regional conference in Dakar, held from 18 to 20 November. The meeting launched a West African process for cooperation on migration and brought together representatives of 15 African countries.

Hammer said Mauritania was directly affected by transatlantic migration flows in West Africa. He listed priorities including stronger border cooperation, national control of immigration data, easier organised migration, modernised border posts and action against document forgery and migrant-smuggling networks.
He said responses required shared responsibility among countries of origin, transit, destination and return. The new process is state-led, with priorities shaped by national choices and needs.

mr.headline: Mauritanian and Spanish armies approve 2027 cooperation programme
mr.dek: The plan followed a review of bilateral military cooperation in 2026 and was approved at a joint commission meeting in Las Palmas on 11 November.
paragraphs: Mauritania’s armed forces and Spain’s military approved a bilateral cooperation programme for 2027 at a joint military commission meeting in Las Palmas, Spain, on 11 November.

The Mauritanian army said the commission reviewed cooperation during 2026 and considered proposed activities for the following year. The meeting was the 25th session of the commission. Mauritania’s delegation was led by Maj. Gen. Sidati Hamadi, head of the army’s human resources division, and included officers from several armed forces formations.
The army announced the outcome in a message on its Facebook page.

mu.headline: Bank of Mauritius sells $15 million as consumer advocate questions results
mu.dek: The November 18 sale brought its 2026 currency interventions to about $170 million, while the rupee lost 2.2% against the dollar from January to October.
paragraphs: The Bank of Mauritius sold $15 million on the domestic foreign-exchange market on November 18, at Rs 46.75, its latest of 12 interventions since the start of 2026. The sales total about $170 million, or nearly Rs 8 billion. Consumer-rights advocate Suttyhudeo Tengur questioned whether the operations have produced concrete benefits for households.

The rupee depreciated 2.2% against the US dollar from January to October, Tengur wrote on Facebook on Friday, November 20. He said occasional dollar injections do not correct underlying imbalances and argued that higher interest rates make credit more expensive, risking further pressure on household purchasing power.
The Monetary Policy Committee raised the Key Rate by 25 basis points to 5.00% on November 11. Annual inflation is projected at 4.7% for December 2026 and 5.5% for December 2027.

mu.headline: Mauritius opposition leader urges PM to intervene over unpaid factory wages
mu.dek: Chetan Baboolall wants the World Knits and Universal Fabrics employees’ case brought before Parliament as workers report months without pay.
paragraphs: Mauritius opposition leader Chetan Baboolall called on Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam to intervene over difficulties facing employees of World Knits and Universal Fabrics at a press conference in Port-Louis on Saturday, 21 November. He said the case should also go before Parliament.

Workers have reported unpaid wages and uncertainty over their jobs for several months. On 2 November, some World Knits employees sought help from lawyer Assad Peeroo; some said they had gone five months without pay, and Peeroo said he would represent them at the Industrial Court. About 475 employees were uncertain about their future after the company entered administration in May.
At Quartier-Militaire on 13 November, World Knits employees rejected liquidation by 374 votes to 31, with eight ballots annulled.

mu.headline: African Union launches Port-Louis credit agency; ratings due by March
mu.dek: The Africa Credit Rating Agency is in talks with 15 governments and plans research in Mauritius, Kenya, Togo, Seychelles and Burundi.
paragraphs: The African Union launched the Africa Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA) on October 7. Based in Port Louis, Mauritius, the agency will assess African governments and corporate borrowers using local data and expertise alongside ratings from international agencies.

Interim chief executive Sifiso Falala said AfCRA is discussing its work with 15 governments, with research planned in Mauritius, Kenya, Togo, the Seychelles and Burundi. The agency expects to issue its first sovereign ratings by the end of March.

A 2023 United Nations Development Programme study estimated that subjectivity in sovereign ratings cost African countries $74.5 billion in excessive interest payments and foregone lending. Moody’s has disputed claims of systematic disadvantage, saying a B-rated sovereign had an estimated one-year default probability of about 5% regardless of region.

mu.headline: Mauritius schedules seven football matches for Sunday
mu.dek: The third round of the 2026-2027 season includes fixtures in the National Super League, National Division Two and National Women’s Super League.
paragraphs: Seven matches are scheduled across Mauritius on Sunday 22 November for the third round of the 2026-2027 football season, organised by the Mauritius Football Association (MFA). The programme spans the National Super League, National Division Two and National Women’s Super League.

Three National Super League matches are set for 15 h 30. La Cure Waves will play P. Rivière Noire FC at Saint-François-Xavier Stadium, with the match broadcast live on FIFA+. Chebel Citizen SC will meet AS Vacoas-Phoenix at Sir Gaëtan Duval Stadium, while Cercle de Joachim faces AS Port-Louis 2000 at New George V Stadium. Mangalkhan SC is scheduled to play the MFA/HPC team at the MFA Astro Pitch.

National Division Two fixtures include El Classico against US Trou aux Biches and CNEF U18 against AS Quatre Bornes, both scheduled for 15 h 30. Sylvester will face La Gaulette Shark at St François Xavier Stadium at 18 h 30.

mu.headline: Port Louis food festival caps dishes at Rs 275
mu.dek: The three-day Waterfront event brings together more than 30 food stands, with concerts and DJ sets scheduled from 19 h to 21 h.
paragraphs: The second Port-Louis Waterfront Food Festival is running through Sunday evening in Mauritius’ capital, bringing food stands, music and leisure activities to the waterfront. Organised by Défi Digital and Radio Plus with the Port Louis Waterfront, the event began Friday.

More than 30 stands offer Mauritian, Indian, Asian and Western dishes, from briani and curries to dumplings, grilled food and desserts. Organisers set a maximum price of Rs 275 per dish. Radio Plus is running games and gift giveaways, while a Kids’ Corner provides activities for children.
Concerts and DJ sets are scheduled from 19 h to 21 h on Saturday and Sunday. Local restaurateurs and artisans are also presenting their specialties at the festival.

mz.headline: Mozambique's only active cashew factory, in Macia, faces threat to 600 jobs
mz.dek: Of the 16 cashew-processing plants that once ran in Mozambique, only the Macia factory in Gaza province is still operating, and it is in serious trouble.
paragraphs: The cashew-processing factory in Macia, Gaza province, is the only one of 16 processing plants that once operated in Mozambique still in activity. It faces serious financial and operating difficulties that put about 600 jobs at risk.
Industrialists in the sector point to the export of raw cashew nuts as a major problem for processing in the country, according to O Pais.

mz.headline: Mondlane denies inciting violence as prosecutors question him
mz.dek: The opposition leader acknowledged calling demonstrations after Mozambique’s disputed 2024 elections but challenged prosecutors to link his actions to specific crimes.
paragraphs: Venâncio Mondlane, Mozambique’s opposition leader, denied inciting violence or property destruction as prosecutors questioned him at the Supreme Court on Thursday. He acknowledged calling demonstrations after the disputed 2024 elections and said his appeal to supporters to take power was a political metaphor.

Mondlane blamed infiltrators and security-force members for the violence, and challenged prosecutors to show how his actions caused the country’s economic difficulties. Prosecutors must establish a connection between his instructions and specific crimes committed during the unrest.

President Daniel Chapo said rebuilding public infrastructure damaged in the protests would cost more than MZN3 billion ($47m). During a visit to Namacurra, in Zambézia province, he said the money could otherwise finance schools, health centres and other public services.

mz.headline: Mozambique starts mobile eye clinic to reach 7,000 rural people
mz.dek: The health ministry and the Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity will run the clinic across five provinces over six months.
paragraphs: Over six months, an estimated 7,000 people in rural communities are expected to receive eye care from a mobile clinic. The service will cover screening, diagnosis and treatment.
The clinic will travel across five provinces, following a route from Maputo to Pemba. The programme is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Health and the Mohamed bin Zayed Foundation for Humanity.
The route takes the clinic the length of the country, reaching communities along the way that have limited access to eye care.

na.headline: Nandi-Ndaitwah urges youth to prepare for Dangote project contracts
na.dek: The president says young businesses should build capacity and partnerships to compete for subcontracts on a planned N$42-billion tank farm and pipeline.
paragraphs: Namibia's President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah has told young entrepreneurs to get ready to bid for subcontracts on the planned N$42-billion Dangote Namibia tank farm and regional pipeline. Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote launched the fuel storage and pipeline project at Walvis Bay earlier this month.

Speaking on Wednesday at the opening of the inaugural National Youth Trade Forum in Windhoek, Nandi-Ndaitwah said young firms should build capacity, form partnerships and learn the procurement requirements. The work on offer spans building, engineering, haulage, equipment upkeep and the supply of goods and services.

She added that young people should not wait for jobs to appear, urging them to develop their own products and look at agriculture, mining, energy, oil and gas, tourism, fisheries, transport and logistics. Industries of that kind, she said, should not serve only established companies and large investors.

na.headline: Miss Namibia unveils bee-eater costume for Miss Universe
na.dek: The national costume is inspired by the Southern Carmine Bee-eater, a bird found along Namibia’s Zambezi River, and features crimson, teal and black colours.
paragraphs: The Miss Namibia Organisation has unveiled the national costume that Charene Labuschagne, Miss Universe Namibia 2026, will wear at the 75th Miss Universe competition in Puerto Rico on 24 November.

The design takes its inspiration from the Southern Carmine Bee-eater, a bird found along Namibia’s Zambezi River. The organisation said the costume reflects the country’s natural beauty, resilience and cultural heritage, and its crimson, teal and black colours match the bird’s striking appearance.
A netted headdress and flowing train symbolise the threat of poaching and the need to protect the species, the organisation said.

na.headline: King Tee Dee plans businesses and community projects to outlast his music
na.dek: The Namibian musician, once known as The Dogg, says his shift in stage name reflects more experience and a wider vision.
paragraphs: Namibian musician and businessman Martin Morocky, who performs as King Tee Dee and was formerly known as The Dogg, says he is building businesses and community projects he expects to last beyond him. He describes the change in name as a move from a young artist proving himself to a businessman focused on long-term growth.

Across two decades in Namibia's kwaito and hip-hop scene, Morocky has released many albums and headlined large festivals across southern Africa. He says sustaining a career that long meant adjusting to shifts in the music market and in his own priorities.
Morocky says fans still call him The Dogg because they grew up with those songs, and that he does not object. He says he is proud of where he started.

ne.headline: ProDAF supplies farm inputs to more than 350 Diffa-region producers
ne.dek: The package includes 10 tonnes of fertiliser, 80 litres of pesticides and seeds for rice, wheat, maize and vegetables.
paragraphs: The Family Farming Development Project (ProDAF) is supplying agricultural inputs to more than 350 producers in the departments of Diffa, Mainé-Soroa and Goudoumaria, in Niger’s Diffa region. The package is intended to support farms using developed and rehabilitated irrigation sites.

It includes 5 tonnes of rice seed, 4 tonnes each of wheat and maize seed, and 7 kilograms of vegetable seed for cabbage, onion, tomato, pepper and watermelon. Producers also receive 10 tonnes of fertiliser and 80 litres of pesticides. Project officials put the total cost at CFA15 million.

The inputs are being distributed across sites in all three departments, including Chétimari, Bitoamaram and Gaouri. ProDAF says the support is intended to strengthen producers’ means of production and make better use of investments in irrigation facilities.

ne.headline: Zinder women's groups mobilise contributions for Niger solidarity fund
ne.dek: The campaign backs President Abdourahamane Tiani's call for each person to contribute CFA100 to the Fund for the Safeguarding of the Homeland.
paragraphs: Women's groups in Zinder, Niger, mobilised resources for the Fund for the Safeguarding of the Homeland at an event on Friday, 20 November, organised by the Mata Massu Doubara ambassadors. Aïssa Amadou Moudiéli, representing the Zinder regional governor, praised the campaign and said it followed the president's appeal. Hadjia Mariama Maman, president of the ambassadors, urged women's groups to contribute. Maman thanked the development partners and non-governmental organisations attending, including CARE, formerly the Cooperative for Assistance and Relief Everywhere, and AFB, a partner organisation named in the report.

rw.headline: MTN Rwanda reports Rwf167.5 billion in first-half service revenue
rw.dek: The operator had 8.7 million subscribers by the end of June, as active data and Mobile Money users also increased.
paragraphs: MTN Rwanda reported Rwf167.5 billion in service revenue for the first half of 2026, up from Rwf137.4 billion in the same period a year earlier. Its subscriber base reached 8.7 million by the end of June, according to the company’s half-year results.

Active data subscribers totalled 2.7 million, while active Mobile Money users reached 6.4 million. The company said the figures covered the six months ended June 30, 2026; profit after tax was Rwf17.2 billion, compared with Rwf5.9 billion a year earlier.

rw.headline: Rwanda's EAX builds storage and quality systems to cut crop losses
rw.dek: The Kigali-based exchange has added warehouses, dryers and farmer training to help produce meet market standards and reach buyers.
paragraphs: The East Africa Exchange (EAX), a commodities marketplace headquartered in Kigali, has invested in certified warehouses, silos and mechanical dryers while training Rwandan farmers and cooperatives in storage, handling and quality. The exchange was established in 2013 to address problems including fragmented markets, post-harvest losses and inconsistent standards.

EAX Chief Executive Clement Kayitakire said maize production lost up to 30% after harvest in the exchange’s early years. Field officers now test produce for moisture and aflatoxin, help grade it and train farmers in drying, cleaning and storage. EAX says trucks rejected at its facilities for poor quality have fallen significantly as farmers learn market requirements.

At its facilities, the exchange inspects deliveries and can dry, clean, sort or re-bag commodities that need corrective work. It monitors stored stocks for moisture changes and infestation, and isolates produce with uncorrectable problems or food-safety risks.

rw.headline: Rwanda security minister studies Suez Canal operations in Egypt
rw.dek: Vincent Biruta and Rwanda's ambassador to Egypt received briefings on the waterway's operations, trade role and maritime security.
paragraphs: Rwanda’s Minister of Internal Security, Vincent Biruta, visited Egypt’s Suez Canal with Rwanda’s ambassador to Egypt, Commissioner General Dan Munyuza, to learn about its operations and role in trade and security. The delegation was received by Suez Canal Authority Chairman Osama Rabie, who briefed them on the waterway’s history and operations.

Biruta was shown canal activities and visited the Suez Canal Museum, where he heard about the waterway’s construction and expansion to handle larger vessels. He said the delegation valued learning about the canal’s history, operations and contribution to international trade and maritime security.

The canal links the Mediterranean and Red seas, connecting shipping between Europe, Asia and other markets. The visit was intended to give the Rwandan delegation insights into managing strategic infrastructure.

Uganda’s Foreign Affairs Ministry outlined activities including rhino tracking, chimpanzee and gorilla trekking, and wildlife safaris. The group is also due to visit Lake Bunyonyi and Kampala. The initiative is intended to promote Uganda as a tourism destination and strengthen cross-border partnerships, according to Taarifa Rwanda.
The trip is also linked to Uganda’s Tenfold Growth Strategy, the outlet reported. The source did not provide a financial target or say whether tour operators had agreed commercial deals.

rw.headline: Kepler College graduate urges class to turn skills to community problems
rw.dek: Oceane Kamikazi told the college's second graduating class that they were trained to create solutions, not wait for them, and that the discipline they built should be used across.
paragraphs: Oceane Kamikazi, speaking for the Class of 2026 at Kepler College in Kigali, urged graduates to use what they learned to address challenges in their communities and across Africa. She said the three-year course had tested students with deadlines, presentations and demanding group assignments.

Kamikazi, who graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in Project Management, recalled struggling to reach a typing speed of 50 words per minute in her first trimester. After scores of 44, 42 and 45 words per minute, she made one final attempt and reached the target. She said the experience taught her staying power, and that classmates learned to help one another when someone fell behind.

The graduation was the college's second and the 11th cohort to graduate through its partnership with Southern New Hampshire University. At the same ceremony, Minister of Sports Nelly Mukazayire urged the 322 graduates from eight African countries to stay teachable and keep up regular exercise.

st.headline: China cites solar systems, roads and rice in São Tomé cooperation
st.dek: China’s ambassador says projects include 3.100 household solar systems serving 40 rural communities and rehabilitated roads in two districts.
paragraphs: China’s ambassador to São Tomé and Príncipe, Xu Yingzhen, cited farming, solar power, road and rice projects as results of cooperation with the island nation in an article published on November 20. She said 25 families in Caldeiras village had increased income through improved crop cultivation and poultry raising with Chinese technology.

Xu said 3.100 household photovoltaic systems were serving 40 rural communities through the “Africa Solar Belt” project. Road works included rehabilitation of 11 kilometres of roads and 2,5 kilometres of drainage in Água Grande and Mé-Zóchi districts. She also said rice from China had been served to vulnerable families, but the article’s quantity is not included here.

China plans to support São Tomé and Príncipe’s National Sustainable Development Strategy 2026-2040 and deepen cooperation in agriculture, energy, infrastructure and livelihoods, Xu wrote. The article also described China’s Global Development Initiative, launched by President Xi Jinping on 21 September 2021.

sn.headline: Senegal's sanitation office blames roadworks for sewer disruptions
sn.dek: The National Sanitation Office (ONAS) says Dakar municipality repairs have buried or damaged inspection chambers, while the city mayor blames the agency for delayed works.
paragraphs: Senegal's National Sanitation Office (ONAS), the state agency that runs the country's sewer and rainwater networks, rejected Dakar Mayor Abass Fall's accusations that it caused delays in municipal works, in a statement responding to his remarks at a press conference on Friday 20 November. Fall had blamed ONAS for delays to some planned work in the capital.

ONAS said road rehabilitation by the municipality has sometimes buried, damaged or blocked sewer inspection chambers with gravel and rubble. The agency said such damage can disrupt sewer networks and cause wastewater overflows on public roads and in some homes. It said it had repeatedly dealt with these incidents without publicly assigning the municipality full responsibility.

The agency manages 2 227 kilometres of wastewater network and 379,5 kilometres for rainwater, and said parts of Dakar's wastewater system are old and suffer recurring pipe breaks. ONAS said work to renew the Hann-Fann collector was at an advanced stage.
